links.outcome: Effect of retrieval-augmented generation on variant classification accuracy
links.effect: Prompt engineering significantly improved accuracy, while RAG further enhanced performance. Accuracy of GPT-4o in distinguishing clinically relevant variants from VUS was 0.7318 (baseline).
links.quote: Prompt engineering significantly improved accuracy, while retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) further enhanced performance.

links.outcome: Output consistency across 100 repeated runs of variant classification
links.effect: Stability analysis across 100 iterations revealed greater consistency with the CIViC system than with OncoKB, with greater inconsistencies for variants with weaker evidence.
links.quote: Stability analysis across 100 iterations revealed greater consistency with the CIViC system than with OncoKB.

links.outcome: Accuracy of LLM clinical knowledge on variant actionability versus expert annotations
links.effect: GPT-4o accuracy 0.7318, Qwen 2.5 0.5731, Llama 3.1 0.4976 in distinguishing clinically relevant variants from VUS; all models tended to overclassify to higher evidence levels.
links.quote: All three models showed a tendency to assign variants to higher evidence levels, suggesting a propensity for overclassification.

unlisted_practices: Prompt engineering to improve LLM classification accuracy

screen.reason: The study benchmarks LLMs for classifying cancer genetic variants and tests the effect of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and prompt engineering as safeguards/deployment practices to improve accuracy.
